title: WPMS/3194/2017 of Bansidhar Sharma Vs District Magistrate/collector Bageshwar AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPMS No. 3194 of 2017
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. S.K. Pandey, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Ms. Mamta Bisht, Brief Holder for
the State.
Mr. Ajay Bisht, Advocate for
respondent No. 3.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
Pursuant to order of the Court
passed on 15.12.2017, respondent No.
3 has been served, therefore, defect as
pointed out by the Registry, stands
cured.
Petitioner is a businessman, who
took cash credit limit of Rs. 20 Lakhs
from Allahabad Bank, Bageshwar
Branch in the year 2014. It appears
that due to some personal difficulty,
petitioner could not repay the amount
in time. Consequently, outstanding
liability of the petitioner has exceeded
the limit by about Rs. 2,82,000/-.
Pursuant to the recovery
certificate issued by the Bank,
Tehsildar has issued a recovery
citation for recovery of Rs. 22,82,623/-
plus other charges.
Thus, feeling aggrieved, petitioner
has approached this Court. The
principal contention of learned counsel
for the petitioner is that since the cash
credit limit is purely a commercial
loan, therefore, the recovery citation
issued against the petitioner is
arbitrary and illegal. However, he fairly

admits that petitioner is liable to repay
the outstanding amount, for which
petitioner wants re-schedulement of
the loan.
Learned counsel appearing for the
Bank submits that if petitioner
approaches Branch Manager of the
Bank by making appropriate
representation along with some
substantial amount, then the Branch
Manager will look into the matter
sympathetically and take appropriate
decision.
Accordingly, the writ petition is
disposed of with liberty to the
petitioner to approach the Branch
Manager concerned by making an
application within ten days from today.
If such an application is made by the
petitioner, the Branch Manager
concerned shall examine petitionerís
request and pass appropriate order, in
accordance with law, within two weeks
thereafter.
Till decision on petitionerís
application, no coercive action shall be
taken against him, pursuant to the
impugned recovery citation. However,
if petitioner fails to make any
application within stipulated time,
then he shall not be entitled to
protection of this order.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
 22.12.2017
Ujjwal
